# Blackbox

> Open-source ESP32-C3 vehicle telemetry: GPS + WT901 IMU, Rust sensor fusion, browser dashboard, circuit/stage lap timing, and local recordings.

## Project
- [Website and USB installer](https://jctoledo.github.io/blackbox/): project overview and verified published firmware installation.
- [Source repository](https://github.com/jctoledo/blackbox): maintained code, README, issues, and contribution history.
- [Releases](https://github.com/jctoledo/blackbox/releases): published firmware; releases can lag main.

## Documentation
- [Lap timer](https://jctoledo.github.io/blackbox/guides/lap-timer.html): record tracks, arm timing, and troubleshoot missed starts.
- [Sensor fusion](https://jctoledo.github.io/blackbox/guides/sensor-fusion.html): frames, prediction, correction, and limitations.
- [How Blackbox works](https://jctoledo.github.io/blackbox/guides/engineering-review.html): architecture, timing, local data ownership, and verification.

## Capabilities and evidence
Blackbox supports circuit/stage timing, interpolated fresh-fix crossings, position-matched references, CSV export, and validated backup/restore. Configuration targets are 25 Hz GPS with NEO-M9N (5 Hz with NEO-6M) and configurable WT901 output up to 200 Hz. No project subscription or cloud account is required.

- [Build or buy comparison](https://jctoledo.github.io/blackbox/guides/comparison.html): documented capabilities alongside RaceBox, RaceChrono Pro, and Performance Box Touch; cost assumptions and proposed features are separate from delivered features.

## Accuracy and status
Blackbox is in active development. Millisecond timestamps and interpolated crossings are not millisecond physical-accuracy claims. The estimator uses diagonal covariance, not a full covariance EKF. Synthetic tests and cross-compilation do not substitute for reference-timed driving or a real USB flash/boot test. Rates depend on configured hardware and measured processing cadence.

This file is a convenient reading index, not a crawler directive or a guarantee of search or AI inclusion.

- [Hardware acceptance checklist](https://jctoledo.github.io/blackbox/guides/hardware-validation.html): bench, USB, sensors, crossings, accuracy, and recording tests.
- [Compatibility and accuracy FAQ](https://jctoledo.github.io/blackbox/guides/faq.html): supported configurations and explicit limits.
- [Interactive dashboard demo](https://jctoledo.github.io/blackbox/demo.html): synthetic telemetry, not a measurement or accuracy demonstration.

- [Experimental mount alignment](https://jctoledo.github.io/blackbox/guides/mount-alignment.html): signed GPS braking evidence, reviewed candidates, persistent save and physical limitations.

- [GPS timestamp logging](https://jctoledo.github.io/blackbox/guides/gps-logging.html): receiver UTC, device parse times, bounded capture, export and offline interval analysis.

- [Maths and hardware rates](https://jctoledo.github.io/blackbox/guides/maths-and-rates.html): interpolation, update-rate budgets, estimator limits, force estimates and calibration assumptions.

- [Rolling intervals](https://jctoledo.github.io/blackbox/guides/rolling-runs.html): 45–70 mph, 30–60 mph and 50–100 km/h receiver-time estimates, validity gates and evidence export; not validated drag timing.

- [Build Blackbox](https://jctoledo.github.io/blackbox/guides/build.html): current C3 parts and signal mapping, mounting, bench checks and assembly photo journal.
